![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14225003/assets/e6c13f4405c407123973c370a20c88b9c989bd54ade909b06414eabc22f0d45e.png)

Consider the vector field $F(x,y,z)=⟨3x+4y,\,3y-4x,\,3z⟩$ and the boundary $S$ of a spherical solid of radius $1$ centered at the origin. Calculate the flux of $F$ through $S.$
question.worked_solution:
If $S$ is an oriented surface with unit normal vector $n,$ and $F$ is continuous vector field, then the flux of $F$ across $S$ measured with respect to $n$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={∬}_{S}F\cdot n\,\text{d}S.
$$

For a sphere or radius $r$ centered at $O,$ the unit normal to the sphere is given by

$$
n=\frac{⟨x,y,z⟩}{r}.
$$

In our case, we have $r=1.$ Therefore,

$$
n=⟨x,y,z⟩.
$$

Using the fact that ${x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}=1$ on $S,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}F\cdot n & =⟨3x+4y,\,3y-4x,\,3z⟩\cdot ⟨x,y,z⟩ \\  & =x(3x+4y)+y(3y-4x)+3{z}^{2} \\  & =3{x}^{2}+4xy+3{y}^{2}-4xy+3{z}^{2} \\  & =3({x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}) \\  & =3\cdot 1 \\  & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can calculate the flux of $F$ across $S$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{S}F\cdot n\,\text{d}S \\  & ={∬}_{S}3\,\text{d}S \\  & =3{∬}_{S}\,\text{d}S \\  & =3\cdot \text{Area}(S) \\  & =3\cdot 4\pi \cdot {1}^{2} \\  & =12\pi \end{aligned}
$$
